---
title: Shape Marginalization by Spectral Panels
---

This page describes [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral]], which computes the marginal
of the observed ellipticity over the intrinsic one,
$$
P(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} \mid g) = \int_{|\chi_I|<1} \mathrm{d}^2\chi_I\,
P_\mathrm{pop}(\chi_I)\, N_2\big(\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} - f_g(\chi_I);\,
\sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2\big) ,
\tag{1}
$$
where $P_\mathrm{pop}$ is the isotropic density of the intrinsic ellipticity $\chi_I$,
$f_g$ the shear map of the ellipticity convention, $g$ the reduced shear and $N_2$ the
isotropic two-dimensional Gaussian of variance $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2$ per component. The
integral is computed by [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]], described in
[Spectral Integration on a Disc](../../../ncm/algebra/spectral_polar.qmd), in the polar
coordinates of a variable of integration $\zeta$ that depends on the ellipticity
convention, defined in [The Variable of Integration](#the-variable-of-integration).

## The Shear Modulus

The integral depends on the shear through its modulus and through the angle between $g$
and $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$. Three cases are separated before anything is integrated.

- $|g| = 1$: every point of the open disc maps to $g$, and
  $P = N_2 (\epsilon_\mathrm{obs} - g; \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2)$.
- $|g| > 1$: for an isotropic population the integral equals the one at $g / |g|^2$, which
  has the same phase and modulus $1 / |g|$. That shear replaces $g$.
- The frame is rotated by the phase $\varphi$ of $g$: with $t \equiv |g| < 1$ and
  $\epsilon \equiv \epsilon_\mathrm{obs} e^{-i \varphi}$, Eq. (1) is the same integral
  with the real shear $t$ and the observed ellipticity $\epsilon$, since
  $f_g (\chi) = e^{i \varphi} f_t (\chi e^{-i \varphi})$ and $P_\mathrm{pop}$ is isotropic.

## The Variable of Integration

For `NC_GALAXY_WL_OBS_ELLIP_CONV_TRACE_DET` the integral is computed in $\chi_I$. For
`NC_GALAXY_WL_OBS_ELLIP_CONV_TRACE` it is computed in the trace--determinant ellipticity
of the same intrinsic shape. This section defines that variable, writes Eq. (1) in it and
states why it is used.

### The two ellipticities of one shape

A shape with axis ratio $q \le 1$ and orientation $\varphi_s$ has the trace ellipticity
$\chi_s$ and the trace--determinant ellipticity $\epsilon_s$ of
[Galaxy Shapes and Ellipticity Frames](wl_ellipticity.qmd),
$$
\chi_s = \frac{1 - q^2}{1 + q^2} \, e^{2 i \varphi_s} ,
\qquad
\epsilon_s = \frac{1 - q}{1 + q} \, e^{2 i \varphi_s} .
$$
They have the same phase, and eliminating $q$ gives $\chi_s = T (\epsilon_s)$ with
$$
T (w) \equiv \frac{2 w}{1 + |w|^2} ,
\qquad
T^{-1} (w) = \frac{w}{1 + \sqrt{1 - |w|^2}} .
$$
$T$ maps the open unit disc onto itself and the unit circle onto itself. For the moduli,
$|T (w)| = u (|w|)$ with
$$
u (r) \equiv \frac{2 r}{1 + r^2} ,
\qquad
1 - u (r) = \frac{(1 - r)^2}{1 + r^2} ,
\qquad
u' (r) = \frac{2 (1 - r^2)}{(1 + r^2)^2} .
\tag{2}
$$

### The shear map

The shear acts on the shape, so the maps of the two conventions are one operation written
in the two ellipticities. With $t < 1$ real, the trace--determinant map is
$$
m_t (w) \equiv \frac{w + t}{1 + t w} ,
$$
and the trace map is
$$
f_t (w) = \frac{w + 2 t + t^2 \bar{w}}{1 + t^2 + 2 t \, \mathrm{Re} \, w}
= T \big( m_t (T^{-1} (w)) \big) .
\tag{3}
$$
The second equality was checked numerically on $10^4$ random pairs $(t, w)$ to
$2 \times 10^{-15}$. The class evaluates $m_t$ with
[[numcosmo|nc_wl_ellipticity_apply_shear_trace_det_real]] for both conventions.

### Eq. (1) in the trace--determinant ellipticity

For the trace convention, let $\epsilon_I \equiv T^{-1} (\chi_I) = r e^{i \theta}$. The
angle is the one of $\chi_I$, and the population is isotropic, so only the density of the
modulus changes. $P_\mathrm{pop}$ is the density of $|\chi_I|$, normalized in
$\mathrm{d} |\chi_I|$, written as its two end power laws times a function that is finite
at both ends,
$$
P_\mathrm{pop} (|\chi_I|) = |\chi_I|^{\alpha_o} (1 - |\chi_I|)^{\alpha_1} \, \hat{P}_\mathrm{pop} (|\chi_I|) ,
$$
with $\alpha_o$ given by [[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_pop_exponent_at_origin]], $\alpha_1$
by [[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_pop_exponent_at_one]] and $\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop}$ by
[[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_pop_eval_p_reduced]]. The density of $r$ is
$P_\mathrm{pop} (u (r)) \, u' (r)$, and with Eq. (2)
$$
P_\mathrm{pop} (u (r)) \, u' (r) = r^{\alpha_o} (1 - r)^{2 \alpha_1 + 1} \, \hat{P}_\epsilon (r) ,
\qquad
\hat{P}_\epsilon (r) \equiv \frac{2^{\alpha_o + 1} (1 + r)}{(1 + r^2)^{\alpha_o + \alpha_1 + 2}} \,
\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop} (u (r)) .
\tag{4}
$$
The three factors of the left side contribute as follows:
$u^{\alpha_o} = 2^{\alpha_o} r^{\alpha_o} (1 + r^2)^{-\alpha_o}$,
$(1 - u)^{\alpha_1} = (1 - r)^{2 \alpha_1} (1 + r^2)^{-\alpha_1}$ and
$u' = 2 (1 - r) (1 + r) (1 + r^2)^{-2}$. The exponent at $r = 1$ changes from $\alpha_1$
to $2 \alpha_1 + 1$, and $\hat{P}_\epsilon$ is finite at both ends. With Eq. (3), Eq. (1)
becomes
$$
P = \int_0^{2 \pi} \!\! \int_0^1 r^{\alpha_o} (1 - r)^{2 \alpha_1 + 1} \,
\frac{\hat{P}_\epsilon (r)}{2 \pi} \,
N_2 \big( \epsilon - T (m_t (r e^{i \theta})); \, \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2 \big) \,
\mathrm{d}r \, \mathrm{d}\theta .
$$
Nothing is approximated: it is Eq. (1) after the substitution $\chi_I = T (\epsilon_I)$.

### Why this variable

Let $\delta \equiv 1 - t$. The two forms of the map are compared near $|g| = 1$, where
every point of the disc except a neighborhood of $-1$ maps close to $g$.

- In $\epsilon_I$: $m_t (\epsilon_I) - 1 = -\delta \, (1 - \epsilon_I) / (1 + t \epsilon_I)$.
  The denominator is zero at $\epsilon_I = -1 / t$, at the distance $\delta / t$ from the
  unit circle, so the map varies on the scale $\delta$ around $\epsilon_I = -1$, in $r$
  and in $\theta$.
- In $\chi_I = x + i y$:
  $f_t (\chi_I) = [(1 + t^2) x + 2 t + i (1 - t^2) y] / [\delta^2 + 2 t (1 + x)]$. The
  denominator changes by its own size when $1 + x$ changes by $\delta^2 / 2 t$, so the map
  varies on the scale $\delta^2$ in $r$ around $\chi_I = -1$ and on the scale $\delta$
  in $\theta$.
- The two statements are the same fact: by Eq. (2), the distance $\delta$ to the unit
  circle in $\epsilon_I$ is the distance $\delta^2 / 2$ in $\chi_I$.

The panels of [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]] halve until they resolve the scale of
the integrand, up to [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar:max-depth]]. At $\delta = 10^{-5}$
the scale is $10^{-5}$ in $\epsilon_I$ and $10^{-10}$ in $\chi_I$, where a radius also
keeps only six significant digits of $1 - r$ in double precision.

### The variable $\zeta$ for both conventions

In the sections below $\zeta = r e^{i \theta}$ is the variable of integration, $F_t$ the
map from $\zeta$ to the sheared ellipticity, and $r^{a} (1 - r)^{b} \hat{P}_\zeta (r)$ the
density of $r$:

| | $\zeta$ | $F_t (\zeta)$ | $a$ | $b$ | $\hat{P}_\zeta (r)$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRACE_DET` | $\chi_I$ | $m_t (\zeta)$ | $\alpha_o$ | $\alpha_1$ | $\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop} (r)$ |
| `TRACE` | $T^{-1} (\chi_I)$ | $T (m_t (\zeta))$ | $\alpha_o$ | $2 \alpha_1 + 1$ | $\hat{P}_\epsilon (r)$ of Eq. (4) |

The truncated Gaussian populations have $\alpha_o = 1$ and $\alpha_1 = 0$, and the Beta
population $\alpha_o = \alpha - 1$ and $\alpha_1 = \beta - 1$ with a constant
$\hat{P}_\mathrm{pop}$.

## The Integral in Polar Coordinates

The density of $r$ is normalized in $\mathrm{d}r$, so the area density is that density
divided by $2 \pi r$, and Eq. (1) is
$$
P = e^{-d_0 / 2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2} \int_0^{2\pi} \!\! \int_0^1 r^{a} (1 - r)^{b} \, G (r, \theta) \, \mathrm{d}r \, \mathrm{d}\theta ,
\qquad
G (r, \theta) \equiv \frac{\hat{P}_\zeta (r)}{2 \pi} \,
\frac{e^{-(d (r, \theta) - d_0) / 2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2}}{2 \pi \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2} ,
\tag{5}
$$
with $d (r, \theta) \equiv |\epsilon - F_t (r e^{i \theta})|^2$ and $d_0$ an offset taken
out of the exponent so that $G$ stays in the double range. This is the integral of
[Spectral Integration on a Disc](../../../ncm/algebra/spectral_polar.qmd) with $R = 1$,
the exponents $a$ and $b$ of the table above and the function $G$.

## Locating the Peak

The panels are placed around the peak of the integrand, which is narrow when
$\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ is small. The peak is searched on one ray.

- The center of the noise factor is $c \equiv F_t^{-1} (\epsilon_0)$, with
  $\epsilon_0 = \epsilon$ for $|\epsilon| < 1$ and otherwise the point of the unit circle
  in the direction of $\epsilon$, moved inside by $10^{-12}$. For `TRACE`,
  $F_t^{-1} = m_t^{-1} \circ T^{-1}$. The ray has the angle $\theta_0 \equiv \arg c$.
- $J_1$ and $J_2$ are the radial and the tangential stretch factors of $F_t^{-1}$ at
  $\epsilon_0$, by finite differences. The noise factor has the widths
  $\sigma_\mathrm{noise} J_1$ and $\sigma_\mathrm{noise} J_2$ around $c$.
- The function
  $$
  h (r) \equiv a \ln r + b \ln (1 - r) + \ln \hat{P}_\zeta (r) - \frac{d (r, \theta_0)}{2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2}
  $$
  is evaluated on a scan of the ray: 401 uniform radii, radii at $10^{-k}$ and
  $1 - 10^{-k}$ for $k = 2, \dots, 12$, and $|c|$ plus and minus multiples from $1/4$ to
  $25$ of the two widths. $r_*$ is the maximum of $h$ by golden section between the
  neighbors of the best radius of the scan.
- $d_0$ is the smallest $d (r, \theta_0)$ of the scan.

The edges are those of [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_peak_edges]] for a peak at
$(r_*, \theta_0)$ with the radial half width
$L \equiv \sigma_\mathrm{noise} \min (J_1, J_2)$ and the angular half width $L / r_*$. They
cover the whole disc.

The scan places the panels and sets $d_0$. It does not decide what is integrated: every
panel is accepted by the test of [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]], and a panel where
$G$ is negligible is accepted on its starting grid by the absolute term of that test. A
peak placed wrongly changes the number of evaluations of $G$.

## Result and Errors

The class computes
$$
\ln P = \ln I - \frac{d_0}{2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2} ,
$$
with $I$ the integral of Eq. (5) from [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_integrate]] at
the relative tolerance `reltol` and absolute tolerance zero.
[[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_factor_eval_marginal]] returns $e^{\ln P}$. An integral that
fails with `NCM_SPECTRAL_POLAR_ERROR_MAX_DEPTH`, or a non-finite $\ln P$, aborts with the
population, $\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$, $g$ and $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$ in the message.

## Measured Accuracy

The reference is the Arb tool `tests/tools/nc_galaxy_shape_marginal_arb.c`, which
certifies $\ln P$ with ball arithmetic. On its 20,055 certified points with
$(|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}| - 1) / \sigma_\mathrm{noise} \le 8$ and $|g| \ne 1$ (truncated
Gaussians of width 0.05 to 0.4, seven Beta populations, both conventions,
$\sigma_\mathrm{noise}$ from 0.005 to 1, $|g|$ from 0 to 3, real $g$), the largest
$|\ln P - \ln P_\mathrm{Arb}|$ per convention is:

| `reltol` | `TRACE` | `TRACE_DET` |
|---|---|---|
| $10^{-3}$ | $5.5 \times 10^{-6}$ | $5.0 \times 10^{-7}$ |
| $10^{-4}$ | $8.6 \times 10^{-8}$ | $2.2 \times 10^{-7}$ |
| $10^{-5}$ (default) | $6.9 \times 10^{-9}$ | $3.9 \times 10^{-9}$ |

No point failed. The tolerance bounds the change of the interpolant between grids, which
is why the differences are below it. The points with
$(|\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}| - 1) / \sigma_\mathrm{noise} > 8$ are observations more than
eight noise standard deviations outside the disc; there the class was checked to return a
finite value. The unit test compares 23 certified points, six of them at a complex $g$
not aligned with $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$, within $10^{-7}$.

## Symbols and the Code

| symbol | in `nc_galaxy_shape_factor_spectral.c` |
|---|---|
| $t$, $\epsilon$ | `t`, `e_1` and `e_2` of the kernel |
| $a$, $b$ | `a`, `b` |
| $\alpha_1$ | `b_pop` |
| $2^{\alpha_o + 1}$, $\alpha_o + \alpha_1 + 2$ of Eq. (4) | `dens_norm`, `dens_pow` of the kernel |
| $F_t$, $F_t^{-1}$, $\hat{P}_\zeta$ | `map`, `map_inv`, `p_reduced` |
| $1 / 2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2$ | `c2` |
| $d_0$, $d_0 / 2 \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2$ | `shift` of the seed, `shift_c2` |
| $1 / (2 \pi \sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2) / (2 \pi)$ | `norm` |
| $\theta_0$, $r_*$, $J_1$, $J_2$ | `theta_0`, `r_star`, `J_1`, `J_2` of the seed |
| $h (r)$ | `_nc_galaxy_shape_factor_spectral_h` |
| $G (r, \theta)$ | the two kernel functions, one per convention |

## API Reference

See [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral]] for the class reference.
[[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_factor_spectral_eval_ln_direct]] computes $\ln P$ from a
population and the values of one galaxy, and
[[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_shape_factor_spectral_eval_panels]] also returns the panels the
integral was accepted on, in the polar coordinates of $\zeta$, with their angles in the
frame of $g$ and $\epsilon_\mathrm{obs}$.
